why: A `decl` node with const:true (IR.md §4.2) means the binding never changes; only variables declared with `auto` may be assigned. The check runs at assembly time, not at run time: catching it later would mean a wrong program compiles and only fails when that line is reached. It is one of the few load-time diagnostics the user can actually fix, which is why the assembly stage reports it as a user error rather than a compiler bug.
fix: remove `const`, or assign to a new variable instead
if this IR was not produced by `hermes ir`, regenerate it — a const `decl` followed by an `assign` to it can only come from a hand edit
